"""Build the Hebrew lesson site: _source/<track>/*.md -> <track>/*.html + index.html.

Lessons are original explanations of the topics mapped in ../CURRICULUM.md.
Standard library only.  Run:  python site/_source/build.py
"""
import html
import json
import re
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = SRC.parent

MODULES = [
    ("start", "00-start-here", "מתחילים כאן"),
    ("foundations", "01-foundations", "יסודות: מספרים, זיכרון ו-Assembly"),
    ("cheat-engine", "02-cheat-engine", "סריקת זיכרון עם Cheat Engine"),
    ("re-tools", "03-re-tools", "כלי Reverse Engineering"),
    ("external", "04-external-trainers", "External Trainers"),
    ("injection", "05-dll-injection", "DLL Injection ו-Shellcode"),
    ("hooking", "06-hooking", "Hooking, Pattern Scanning וקריאה לפונקציות"),
    ("rendering", "07-rendering", "Rendering: ESP, Overlays ותפריטים"),
    ("features", "08-features", "בניית יכולות על משחקי תרגול"),
    ("engines", "09-engines", "מנועים ופלטפורמות"),
    ("kernel", "10-kernel", "Kernel"),
    ("anticheat", "11-anticheat-internals", "איך Anti-Cheat ו-Anti-Debug עובדים"),
    ("crackme", "12-crackmes", "CrackMes, KeyGens ו-Unpacking"),
    ("malware", "13-malware-analysis", "Malware Analysis"),
    ("exploit", "14-exploit-dev", "Exploit Development"),
    ("pentest", "15-pentest-ctf", "Pentest ו-CTF"),
]
SITE = "Game Hacking בעברית"

# lesson (track folder/file stem) -> video project under ../videos
VIDEOS = {
    "01-foundations/01-number-bases": "01-number-bases",
    "01-foundations/02-data-types-in-memory": "02-data-types",
    "01-foundations/03-virtual-memory": "03-virtual-memory",
    "01-foundations/04-pointers-and-pointer-chains": "04-pointer-chains",
    "01-foundations/05-reading-assembly": "05-reading-assembly",
    "01-foundations/06-hex-editing-files": "06-hex-editing",
    "01-foundations/07-stack-and-calling-conventions": "07-calling-conventions",
    "01-foundations/08-pe-processes-and-winapi": "08-inside-an-exe",
}


def lesson_video(md_path):
    """Copy the lesson's newest render to site/videos/ and return its player card, or ''."""
    name = VIDEOS.get(f"{md_path.parent.name}/{md_path.stem}")
    renders = sorted((OUT.parent / "videos" / name / "renders").glob("*.mp4")) if name else []
    if not renders:
        return ""
    (OUT / "videos").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(renders[-1], OUT / "videos" / f"{name}.mp4")
    return (f'<section class="card"><h2>סרטון השיעור (באנגלית)</h2>'
            f'<video controls preload="metadata" src="../videos/{name}.mp4" '
            f'style="display:block;width:100%;border-radius:10px;background:#000"></video></section>')


def planned_units():
    """Remake units per track, from the catalog built by ../build_catalog.py."""
    cat = SRC.parent.parent / "catalog.json"
    if not cat.exists():
        return {}
    units = {}
    for v in json.loads(cat.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
        units.setdefault(v["track"], set()).add(v["series"])
    return {t: len(u) for t, u in units.items()}

NOTICE = "לתרגול על משחקי offline בלבד"
SECTION_CLASS = {"הרעיון בקצרה": "tldr", "מילון מונחים": "glossary", "בדיקה עצמית": "quiz"}

THEME_JS = """<script>
(function(){var r=document.documentElement,k='gh-he-theme';
try{var s=localStorage.getItem(k);if(s)r.setAttribute('data-theme',s);}catch(e){}
window.toggleTheme=function(){var d=r.getAttribute('data-theme');
if(!d){d=matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches?'dark':'light';}
var n=d==='dark'?'light':'dark';r.setAttribute('data-theme',n);
try{localStorage.setItem(k,n);}catch(e){}};
addEventListener('scroll',function(){var p=document.querySelector('.progress');if(!p)return;
var h=document.documentElement;var m=h.scrollHeight-h.clientHeight;
p.style.width=(m>0?(h.scrollTop/m*100):0)+'%';},{passive:true});})();
</script>"""


def inline(text):
    """Inline markdown -> HTML (code, links, bold, italic)."""
    codes = []

    def stash(m):
        codes.append(m.group(1))
        return f"\x00{len(codes) - 1}\x00"

    text = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", stash, text)
    text = html.escape(text, quote=False)
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)",
                  r'<a href="\2" target="_blank" rel="noopener">\1</a>', text)
    text = re.sub(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*", r"<strong>\1</strong>", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?<![\w*])\*([^*\s][^*]*?)\*(?![\w*])", r"<em>\1</em>", text)
    return re.sub(r"\x00(\d+)\x00",
                  lambda m: f"<code>{html.escape(codes[int(m.group(1))])}</code>", text)


def cells(line):
    return [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]


def parse(md):
    """Return (title, meta_chips, sections) where sections = [(heading|None, html)]."""
    lines = [l.rstrip() for l in md.splitlines()]
    lines = [l for l in lines if l.strip() not in ('<div dir="rtl">', "</div>")]
    title, chips = "", []
    sections, cur_head, buf = [], None, []

    def flush():
        nonlocal buf
        if cur_head is not None or any(b.strip() for b in buf):
            sections.append((cur_head, "\n".join(buf)))
        buf = []

    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        s = line.strip()
        if not s:
            i += 1
            continue
        if s.startswith("# "):
            title = s[2:].strip()
            i += 1
        elif s.startswith("## "):
            flush()
            cur_head = s[3:].strip()
            i += 1
        elif s.startswith("### "):
            buf.append(f"<h3>{inline(s[4:].strip())}</h3>")
            i += 1
        elif s.startswith("**מודול:**"):
            for part in s.split("·"):
                m = re.match(r"\s*\*\*(.+?)\*\*\s*(.*)", part)
                if m:
                    chips.append((m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()))
            i += 1
        elif s.startswith("```"):
            code = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith("```"):
                code.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            i += 1
            buf.append('<pre dir="ltr"><code>' + html.escape("\n".join(code)) + "</code></pre>")
        elif s.startswith(">"):
            block = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip().startswith(">"):
                block.append(lines[i].strip()[1:].strip())
                i += 1
            paras = "".join(f"<p>{inline(b)}</p>" for b in block if b)
            buf.append(f"<blockquote>{paras}</blockquote>")
        elif s.startswith("|"):
            rows = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip().startswith("|"):
                rows.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            head = cells(rows[0])
            body = [cells(r) for r in rows[2:]]
            t = ['<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr>']
            t += [f"<th>{inline(c)}</th>" for c in head]
            t.append("</tr></thead><tbody>")
            for r in body:
                t.append("<tr>" + "".join(f"<td>{inline(c)}</td>" for c in r) + "</tr>")
            t.append("</tbody></table></div>")
            buf.append("".join(t))
        elif re.match(r"^(-|\d+\.)\s+", s):
            ordered = bool(re.match(r"^\d+\.", s))
            pat = r"^\d+\.\s+" if ordered else r"^-\s+"
            items = []
            while i < len(lines) and re.match(pat, lines[i].strip()):
                items.append(re.sub(pat, "", lines[i].strip()))
                i += 1
            tag = "ol" if ordered else "ul"
            buf.append(f"<{tag}>" + "".join(f"<li>{inline(x)}</li>" for x in items) + f"</{tag}>")
        else:
            para = [s]
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and not re.match(
                    r"^(#|>|\||-\s|\d+\.\s)", lines[i].strip()):
                para.append(lines[i].strip())
                i += 1
            buf.append(f"<p>{inline(' '.join(para))}</p>")
    flush()
    return title, chips, sections


def page(title, body, crumb, root, toc=""):
    layout = "layout" if toc else "layout single"
    return f"""<!doctype html>
<html lang="he" dir="rtl">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>{html.escape(title)}</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{root}assets/style.css">
{THEME_JS}
</head>
<body>
<div class="progress"></div>
<header class="topbar">
  <a class="home" href="{root}index.html">🎮 {SITE}</a>
  <span class="crumb">{crumb}</span>
  <span class="spacer"></span>
  <span class="badge">{NOTICE}</span>
  <button class="theme-btn" onclick="toggleTheme()" title="מצב בהיר / כהה" aria-label="מצב בהיר או כהה">◐</button>
</header>
<div class="{layout}">
<main>
{body}
<footer class="foot">{SITE} · שיעורים מקוריים · {NOTICE}</footer>
</main>
{toc}
</div>
</body>
</html>
"""


def build_lesson(md_path, mod_title, prev, nxt):
    title, chips, sections = parse(md_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    m = re.match(r"(שיעור\s+[\d.]+)\s*[—-]\s*(.+)", title)
    kicker, h1 = (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else ("", title)
    chip_html = "".join(f'<span class="chip">{html.escape(k)} <b dir="auto">{html.escape(v)}</b></span>'
                        for k, v in chips)
    parts = [f'<section class="hero"><div class="kicker">{html.escape(kicker)}</div>'
             f'<h1>{inline(h1)}</h1><div class="chips">{chip_html}</div></section>']
    video = lesson_video(md_path)
    if video:
        parts.append(video)
    toc_links = []
    for n, (head, content) in enumerate(sections):
        if head is None:
            parts.append(f'<section class="card">{content}</section>')
            continue
        cls = SECTION_CLASS.get(head, "")
        parts.append(f'<section class="card {cls}" id="s{n}"><h2>{inline(head)}</h2>\n{content}</section>')
        toc_links.append(f'<a href="#s{n}">{inline(head)}</a>')

    def link(item, cls, label):
        if not item:
            return "<span></span>"
        return f'<a class="{cls}" href="{item[0]}"><small>{label}</small>{html.escape(item[1])}</a>'

    parts.append(f'<nav class="pager">{link(prev, "prev", "→ השיעור הקודם")}'
                 f'{link(nxt, "next", "השיעור הבא ←")}</nav>')
    toc = '<aside class="toc"><div class="toc-title">בעמוד זה</div>' + "".join(toc_links) + "</aside>"
    crumb = f'<span dir="auto">{html.escape(mod_title)}</span>'
    return title, page(title, "\n".join(parts), crumb, "../", toc)


def main():
    index_modules = []
    total = 0
    for num, (track, folder, mod_title) in enumerate(MODULES):
        src_dir = SRC / folder
        files = sorted(src_dir.glob("*.md")) if src_dir.is_dir() else []
        titles = []
        for f in files:
            t, _, _ = parse(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            titles.append(t)
        lessons = []
        for i, f in enumerate(files):
            prev = (files[i - 1].stem + ".html", titles[i - 1]) if i > 0 else None
            nxt = (files[i + 1].stem + ".html", titles[i + 1]) if i + 1 < len(files) else None
            title, doc = build_lesson(f, mod_title, prev, nxt)
            out_dir = OUT / folder
            out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            (out_dir / (f.stem + ".html")).write_text(doc, encoding="utf-8")
            lessons.append((f"{folder}/{f.stem}.html", title))
            total += 1
        index_modules.append((num, track, mod_title, lessons))

    cards = []
    planned = planned_units()
    for num, track, mod_title, lessons in index_modules:
        state = (f"{len(lessons)} שיעורים · " if lessons else "בקרוב · ") + f"{planned.get(track, 0)} יחידות מקור"
        items = "".join(f'<li><a href="{href}">{html.escape(t)}</a></li>' for href, t in lessons)
        ul = f'<ul class="lessons">{items}</ul>' if lessons else ""
        cards.append(f'<div class="module{"" if lessons else " empty"}"><div class="module-head">'
                     f'<span class="module-num">{num:02d}</span>'
                     f'<span class="module-title">{inline(mod_title)}</span>'
                     f'<span class="module-state">{state}</span></div>{ul}</div>')
    body = f"""<section class="hero"><div class="kicker">קורס בעברית</div>
<h1>{SITE}</h1>
<div class="chips"><span class="chip"><b>{len(MODULES)}</b> מסלולים</span><span class="chip"><b>{total}</b> שיעורים עד כה</span></div></section>
<div class="notice"><p><strong>מה יש כאן.</strong> שיעורים מקוריים בעברית על Reverse Engineering ו-Game Hacking, מסודרים לפי סדר לימוד: מיסודות הזיכרון ועד Kernel וניתוח Malware. מונחים מקצועיים נשארים באנגלית, עם הסבר בפעם הראשונה שהם מופיעים.</p>
<p><strong>{NOTICE}.</strong> מתרגלים על משחקי single-player, על משחקי קוד פתוח כמו AssaultCube מול בוטים, ועל תוכנות שכתבתם בעצמכם. לא על משחקים מקוונים ולא נגד שחקנים אחרים.</p></div>
<div class="modules">{''.join(cards)}</div>"""
    (OUT / "index.html").write_text(page(SITE, body, "", ""), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"built {total} lessons + index.html")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="he" dir="rtl">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Game Hacking בעברית</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/style.css">
<script>
(function(){var r=document.documentElement,k='gh-he-theme';
try{var s=localStorage.getItem(k);if(s)r.setAttribute('data-theme',s);}catch(e){}
window.toggleTheme=function(){var d=r.getAttribute('data-theme');
if(!d){d=matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches?'dark':'light';}
var n=d==='dark'?'light':'dark';r.setAttribute('data-theme',n);
try{localStorage.setItem(k,n);}catch(e){}};

`videos/01-number-bases/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# HyperFrames Composition Project

This folder is a [HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) video: HTML, CSS and seekable
animations (GSAP by default) that the `hyperframes` CLI previews in the browser and renders to
MP4.

## Skills — read these first

**Invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that generic web docs don't cover, so compositions written without them break.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes`. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (each kind of film, story, motion, look, sound, review, captions, overlays). Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you.

- `/hyperframes` — read first for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays. Holds the render contract and the work loop.
- `/hyperframes-cli` — the CLI by job: scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render, publish, project history.
- `/hyperframes-registry` — ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source. Search it before hand-building any named visual.
- `/media-use` — get or make any media (music, sound effects, images, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades) and mix placed audio.
- `/reverse-any-video` — rebuild any video file as an editable HyperFrames project and check it against the original frame by frame (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/style-sampling` — make a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/figma` — bring a Figma design, frame, logo or brand into a video.
- `/slideshow` — a presentation or pitch deck. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4.
- `/remotion-to-hyperframes` — bring existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, or renders from other tools) and verify it frame by frame against the original.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `hyperframes-cli/references/init-and-scaffold.md` (Tailwind).

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. The person updates
> the plugin through its plugin manager; the standalone commands below do not apply.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Installing and updating skills is the person's step:
> tell them which skill is missing or stale, and do not run the install yourself. For the user:
> `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` installs/refreshes that skill, and bare
> `npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes the core set plus everything already installed —
> neither pulls the full set. Newly installed skills load in a new agent session.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # human-operated foreground preview (blocks until stopped)
npx hyperframes preview --background  # agent-safe persistent Studio preview
npx hyperframes preview --status      # verify the persistent preview is listening
npx hyperframes preview --stop        # stop it when review is finished
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npx hyperframes snapshot --at 1,3,5  # PNG frames at those seconds, to look at before rendering
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **Agents must use `npx hyperframes preview --background` for Studio handoff.** Do not rely
> on a shell/tool `run_in_background` wrapper around `npm run dev`: that foreground process
> remains owned by the invoking session and can disappear while the browser stays open,
> leaving refreshes at `ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`. Verify with `preview --status`. The desktop
> app can't edit the project while this preview runs, so `npx hyperframes open` stops it first.
> If you hand the project to the app another way, run `preview --stop` before you do. Otherwise keep it
> alive through review, and stop it explicitly with `preview --stop` afterward.

> **Back from the desktop app.** Once this project was opened in the HyperFrames desktop app, run `npx hyperframes catch-up` before your next change here: it lists what the person asked Framey in the app and which files changed since.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

Then look at what you changed: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>` (or `--range START,END`, `--composition <id>`) at the moments you edited, and read the frames before you reply. A passing check does not show how it looks.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start` and a duration. `data-start` is what marks it as timed; `data-track-index` is an optional Studio display lane the render never reads
2. Give timed visual elements `class="clip"`. The framework keys visibility off `data-start`, not the class, but the shared `.clip` CSS is what gives a scene its full-frame box, and `lint` warns without it
3. Register one paused root timeline per composition on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
   Scene timelines manually added to this root must not be paused. A paused
   child does not advance when the root is seeked. The runtime activates
   registered composition siblings, not arbitrary nested scene timelines.
4. A video with sound keeps it on the `<video>` (`data-has-audio="true"`, no `muted`). Use a separate `<audio>` for music, voiceover, replacement audio, J/L cuts, or audio detached in Studio. Silent footage and b-roll: `muted`.
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

```

`videos/01-number-bases/REVIEW.md`:

```md
# Review: Hex, Decimal & Binary (pilot)

## Creative calls
- Storyline A, "The Health Bar". Not built: B "Three Odometers", C "Ten Fingers" (see STORYLINES.md).
- Opens on a steady 100 with the bar filling, instead of a hit to 99, so the followed byte stays 64.
- Arena floor is a flat drawn grid, not a 3D plane (the 3D plane hid the HUD during camera zooms).
- Narration: Azure Speech, en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural at -4%, one clip per shot. Every shot is timed to its clip's word timings. Film length 80.4 s.
- No music and no sound effects: no music source was signed in.

## Measured vs looked at
- Measured: `check` passes with no errors and no warnings; narration clip lengths and word offsets come from Azure.
- Looked at: still frames of every shot and every cut. Not watched at full speed.
- Not checked by anyone: how the narration sounds, and whether picture and voice feel in sync on playback.

## Weakest shot
- Shot 6 (digit table): rows 0-9 arrive in two seconds while the voice says "zero to nine"; readable on pause, quick at speed.
- Shot 2 to 3 cut: the zoomed byte and the arriving tile differ slightly in size and place.

## With more time
- A music bed that drops out inside memory and returns on the pull-back; ticks on the bit cells; one impact on FF.

```

`videos/01-number-bases/SCRIPT.md`:

```md
# Narration — Hex, Decimal & Binary (pilot)

Voiced with Azure Speech (en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural, rate -4%) by ../tools/azure_tts.py. About 175 words, 80.4 s film; the ranges are each shot's slot.

1. (0–8.5) Your health says one hundred. But the game never wrote down a one and two zeros. So what did it store?
2. (8.5–17.6) Dive into the game's memory and you find rows of this: pairs of digits and letters. One pair is your health.
3. (17.6–27.2) This one. Six-four. Not sixty-four: this is hexadecimal, base sixteen, and it means exactly one hundred.
4. (27.2–35.3) Underneath, it is one byte: eight bits, each a zero or a one. That is all the machine really has.
5. (35.3–45.5) Now split the eight bits into two groups of four. The first group is worth six. The second is worth four.
6. (45.5–55.4) Four bits can make sixteen patterns, so you need sixteen digits. Zero to nine, then A through F for ten to fifteen.
7. (55.4–65.1) Fill every bit with a one and both digits become F. F-F is two hundred fifty-five, the most one byte can hold.
8. (65.1–72.9) So write F-F into that byte, climb back out, and your health reads two hundred fifty-five.
9. (72.9–80.4) Hex is not a different number. It is the same bits, four at a time.

```

`videos/01-number-bases/SPEC.md`:

```md
# SPEC — Hex, Decimal & Binary (pilot, storyline A "The Health Bar")

GOAL:    The viewer can look at one hex byte and say "that's two groups of four bits", and knows why memory tools show hex.
OUTPUT:  HyperFrames, 1920 x 1080, 30 fps
TIME:    71.5 s x 30 = 2145 frames. Narrated: the voice is the clock (SCRIPT.md). Bed ~100 bpm = 18 frames per beat.
LOOK:    Two worlds, one palette.
         Outside (game): flat-shaded arena, sky #1C7C8A to #0E4A55 radial, floor tiles #14606B / #0F5560, crates #E8B04A with #B9832E shade.
         Inside (memory): graph paper ground #E4F2EC, grid lines #9CCFC0 at 60 px (major, 3 px) and 20 px (minor, 1 px), ink #0B2A30.
         Accent #FF5A1F: only on the byte being followed and the digits made from it. Never decoration.
         Display: League Gothic 400, HUD numerals 300 px, tracking 0. Titles: Archivo Black, 96-120 px, tracking -1%.
         Data: IBM Plex Mono 700, bytes 46 px in the wall, bit cells 150 px, hero digits 420-520 px.
         Medium: printed graph paper and cut tiles. Tiles have a hard 10 px offset shadow #0B2A30 at 100%, no blur. No grain, no vignette.
OBJECTS: HUD (health bar with segmented fill, big numeral, ammo counter, crosshair); memory wall (address column + 16 byte columns per row);
         byte tile (orange square tile, two hex digits); bit cell (square tile holding 0 or 1, place value 8/4/2/1 printed above);
         digit table (bit pattern -> hex digit, 16 rows in two columns of 8).
MOTION:  enter: power3.out 10 frames, tiles are placed (scale 1.15 -> 1, no fade longer than 4 frames); move: power2.inOut 18 frames;
         camera dive/pull-back: expo.inOut 30 frames; stagger between bit cells 3 frames; text never moves after it lands.
SHOTS:   1  f0-195     HUD world. Hero: push toward the numeral 100. Reads "HEALTH 100" (0.3-3s). Bed in; hands off by diving into the digits.
         2  f195-420   Memory wall. Hero: wall scrolls in row by row, then all bytes dim except 64. Reads address 00F8A4A0 row, byte 64 (3-7s). Bed drops out; key ticks on rows.
         3  f420-645   Byte alone. Hero: 64 tile scales to 45% of frame height. Reads "64" then struck "sixty-four", then "= 100" (2-7s). Pop on "= 100".
         4  f645-870   Eight bits. Hero: tile unfolds into 8 bit cells. Reads 0 1 1 0 0 1 0 0 and "1 byte = 8 bits" (1-7s). Tick per cell.
         5  f870-1140  Split. Hero: the row parts in the middle. Reads place values 8 4 2 1, "4+2 = 6", "4 = 4", then "6x16 + 4 = 100" (2-8.5s). Pop on each digit.
         6  f1140-1410 Digit table. Hero: table grows one row per 6 frames. Reads 0000->0 ... 1111->F, A-F rows in accent (1-8.5s). Soft ticks.
         7  f1410-1680 FF. Hero: every cell flips to 1 left to right. Reads F F, "= 255", "the most one byte can hold" (2-8.5s). Impact on FF.
         8  f1680-1920 Pull back to HUD. Hero: camera pulls out of the byte; numeral reads 255, bar overruns its frame. Reads "255" (2.5-7.5s). Bed returns.
         9  f1920-2145 Claim on graph paper. Reads "Hex is the same bits, four at a time." (1-7.5s). Bed ends on a bar line.
BANNED:  spec.md defaults (dark void, glow/neon, glass cards, everything centred, fade-and-slide-up, corner brackets, three cards in a row),
         plus: Matrix-style falling green code, hacker hoodie imagery, terminal-green-on-black, any real game's HUD or logo, decorative binary rain.
QA:      1.5s HUD numeral readable; 10s the 64 is the only accent in the wall; 18s struck "sixty-four" and "= 100" both legible;
         26s eight cells read 01100100; 35s sums agree (6, 4, 100); 44s 16 rows, A-F correct; 53s FF = 255; 61s HUD says 255; 69s claim holds 2 s+.

```

## Frame 1: The health bar (0-8.5s)

- poster: 3s

- sound: bed enters on its strongest bar; no effects

## Frame 2: The wall of bytes (8.5-17.6s)

- reads: eight cells land left to right (1.0-4.0s); "1 byte = 8 bits" (4.0-7.5s)
- sound: one tick per cell, two takes rotated

## Frame 5: Two groups of four (35.3-45.5s)

- poster: 6s
- transition_in: the same row of cells parts in the middle

- voiceover: "Now split the eight bits into two groups of four. The first group is worth six. The second is worth four."
- reads: the split and 8 4 2 1 (0.5-2.5s); 4 + 2 gives 6 (2.5-5.0s); 4 gives 4 (5.0-6.5s); 6 x 16 + 4 = 100 (6.5-9.0s)
- sound: pop on each digit landing

## Frame 6: Sixteen digits (45.5-55.4s)

- sound: soft ticks while rows arrive, none after

- sound: riser into one impact on FF, the only one in the film

## Frame 8: Back in the game (65.1-72.9s)

- voiceover: "So write F-F into that byte, climb back out, and your health reads two hundred fifty-five."
- reads: FF written at 00F8A4AC (0.5-2.5s); HEALTH 255 (2.5-8.0s)
- sound: bed returns in full on the pull-back

## Frame 9: The one idea (72.9-80.4s)

- sound: bed ends on a bar line with a short fade

`videos/01-number-bases/STORYLINES.md`:

```md
# Storylines — Pilot: Hex, Decimal & Binary

Source: `../../site/_source/01-foundations/01-number-bases.md` (own lesson). Every number below comes from it.

**The one idea:** one hex digit is exactly four bits, so two hex digits are exactly one byte. That is why every memory tool shows hex.

**What the viewer remembers:** "Hex isn't a different number. It's the same bits, four at a time."

**Viewer and task:** a beginner opens a memory viewer for the first time, sees a wall of `E8 03 00 00`, and wants to read it.

**Assumptions:** 75–90 s, 16:9 at 1920×1080, English narration plus a quiet music bed. Voice and music sources are not chosen yet: a free local voice if one is available, otherwise a paid HeyGen voice; music from the catalog needs a HeyGen sign-in, otherwise the film ships with voice only.

---

## A. The Health Bar (recommended)

*Device: a moment in someone's play session. Form: an endless zoom.*

A game HUD shows HEALTH 100. The camera dives into the number and lands in the memory behind it, where the same value is the single byte `64`. The film stays on that one byte and reads it three ways, then comes back out to the HUD and changes it.

- **First two seconds:** a full-frame HUD, health bar full, the number `100` large; a hit lands and it ticks to `99`, then the camera starts pushing into the digits.
- **Beats:** HUD takes a hit → dive into the number, wall of hex bytes → "the game doesn't store 100, it stores this" (`64` isolated) → the byte opens into eight bits `0110 0100` → the bits split into two groups of four, each group becomes one hex digit (`6`, `4`) → the 16-row digit table grows one row at a time only as far as needed → same trick on `FF` = `1111 1111` = 255, the most a byte can hold → pull back out: the byte is overwritten with `FF`, the HUD reads 255 → one line: "Hex is the same bits, four at a time."
- **Look:** saturated arcade HUD world on the outside (deep teal ground, chunky condensed display type), a bright graph-paper memory grid on the inside with mono digits; one accent, hot orange, only on the byte being followed.
- **Sound:** light chiptune-leaning bed at ~100 bpm that drops to near silence inside memory and returns on the pull-back; a soft tick on each bit landing, one impact on `FF`.

## B. Three Odometers

*Device: the object is the explanation. Form: one continuous take.*

Three mechanical counters sit on one workbench, geared together: eight binary wheels, three decimal wheels, two hex wheels. They count the same number in step. The camera drifts along the bench and the viewer watches where each one rolls over.

- **First two seconds:** macro shot of counter wheels mid-roll, clicking from 9 to 10 on the decimal counter while the hex one beside it shows `9` → `A`.
- **Beats:** three counters count from 0 together → decimal rolls over at 10, hex keeps going through A–F → push in: the hex wheel turns once for every full cycle of the four binary wheels under it (a visible gear links them) → count runs fast to 100: `0110 0100` / `100` / `64` → runs to 255: binary and hex both hit their last position (`1111 1111`, `FF`) at the same moment, decimal sits at an awkward `255` → the next click overflows binary and hex together → one line on the bench: "Two hex digits. One byte. Exactly."
- **Look:** warm workshop bench under a single lamp, brass and enamel number wheels, engraved labels; type is a stamped grotesque. No screens anywhere.
- **Sound:** no music until 100; mechanical wheel clicks carry the rhythm, a low pulse enters for the run to 255, one heavy clunk on the overflow.

## C. Ten Fingers (the bold one)

*Device: type carries the argument. Form: cut on the beat.*

No objects at all. Giant kinetic type argues the point: you count in tens because of your hands; the machine has two states; hex is the handshake between you. Colour fields flip on every beat and the digits themselves do the acting.

- **First two seconds:** full-frame `10` in black on yellow; the frame flips and the same `10` is captioned "this is sixteen".
- **Beats:** `10` means ten, then two, then sixteen, depending on the base → a screen-filling wall of `0`s and `1`s, unreadable → the wall is cut by vertical rules every four digits → each four-bit block collapses into a single glyph, the wall shrinks to a quarter of its width → `0x3E8` expands in place to `3×256 + 14×16 + 8 = 1000` → three traps flash as struck-through lines (`0x10 ≠ 10`) → final field: "Same bits. Four at a time."
- **Look:** flat poster colour fields (yellow, black, signal red), one heavy condensed sans at huge sizes, mono only for the bit wall.
- **Sound:** driving minimal percussion at ~128 bpm, every cut on a hit; narration is sparse, about half the words of A or B.

```

`videos/01-number-bases/build.py`:

```py
"""One-off: write the animated scene files from the approved storyboard layouts. Outputs are plain HTML, edited by hand afterwards."""
from pathlib import Path

P = Path(r"C:\ai\gh-remake\videos\01-number-bases")
C = P / "compositions"

PAPER_BG = """background-color: #E4F2EC;
      background-image:
        linear-gradient(#9CCFC0 3px, transparent 3px), linear-gradient(90deg, #9CCFC0 3px, transparent 3px),
        linear-gradient(#C4E3D9 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, #C4E3D9 1px, transparent 1px);
      background-size: 60px 60px, 60px 60px, 20px 20px, 20px 20px;"""

PAPER = f"""
    #root {{ position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; {PAPER_BG}
      font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; color: #0B2A30; }}
    .{{p}}-stage {{ position: absolute; inset: 0; }}
"""

ARENA = """
    #root { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; color: #fff; font-family: 'League Gothic', sans-serif; background: #0E4A55; }
    .{p}-stage { position: absolute; inset: 0; }
    .{p}-cam { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 38%, #2A97A6 0%, #1C7C8A 35%, #0E4A55 100%); }
    .{p}-world { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 0; isolation: isolate; }
    .{p}-wall { position: absolute; left: -200px; right: -200px; top: 330px; height: 150px; background: #0C4650; border-top: 10px solid #093840; }
    .{p}-floorwrap { position: absolute; left: -200px; right: -200px; top: 480px; bottom: 0; overflow: hidden; background: #0F5560; }
    .{p}-floor { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
    .{p}-crate { position: absolute; z-index: 2; background: #E8B04A; border: 10px solid #B9832E; box-shadow: 14px 14px 0 #093840; }
    .{p}-crate::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0;
      background: linear-gradient(45deg, transparent 47%, #B9832E 47%, #B9832E 53%, transparent 53%); }
    .{p}-cross { position: absolute; left: 960px; top: 470px; width: 0; height: 0; z-index: 4; }
    .{p}-cross i { position: absolute; background: #fff; }
    .{p}-cross i:nth-child(1) { left: -34px; top: -3px; width: 22px; height: 6px; }
    .{p}-cross i:nth-child(2) { left: 12px; top: -3px; width: 22px; height: 6px; }
    .{p}-cross i:nth-child(3) { left: -3px; top: -34px; width: 6px; height: 22px; }
    .{p}-cross i:nth-child(4) { left: -3px; top: 12px; width: 6px; height: 22px; }
    .{p}-hud { position: absolute; left: 192px; bottom: 108px; z-index: 5; }
    .{p}-label { font-size: 64px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; line-height: 1; }
    .{p}-num { font-size: 330px; line-height: 0.86; margin-top: 6px; }
    .{p}-bar { position: relative; margin-top: 18px; width: 560px; height: 46px; border: 8px solid #fff; background: #093840; }
    .{p}-fill { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; background: #FF5A1F;
      background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 50px, #093840 50px); background-size: 56px 100%; }
"""

ARENA_WORLD = """
        <div id="{p}-world" class="{p}-world" data-layout-allow-overflow>
          <div class="{p}-wall"></div>
          <div class="{p}-floorwrap"><svg class="{p}-floor" viewBox="0 0 2320 600" preserveAspectRatio="none"><rect width="2320" height="600" fill="#14606B"/><g stroke="#0C4650" stroke-width="6"><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-3600" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-3260" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-2920" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-2580" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-2240" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-1900" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-1560" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-1220" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-880" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-540" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="-200" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="140" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="480" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="820" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="1160" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="1500" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="1840" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="2180" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="2520" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="2860" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="3200" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="3540" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="3880" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="4220" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="4560" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="4900" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="5240" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="5580" y2="600"/><line x1="1160" y1="-150" x2="5920" y2="600"/><line x1="0" y1="18" x2="2320" y2="18"/><line x1="0" y1="48" x2="2320" y2="48"/><line x1="0" y1="96" x2="2320" y2="96"/><line x1="0" y1="172" x2="2320" y2="172"/><line x1="0" y1="300" x2="2320" y2="300"/><line x1="0" y1="520" x2="2320" y2="520"/></g></svg></div>
          <div class="{p}-crate" style="left: 1210px; top: 380px; width: 230px; height: 230px"></div>
          <div class="{p}-crate" style="left: 1470px; top: 450px; width: 170px; height: 170px"></div>
          <div class="{p}-crate" style="left: 330px; top: 410px; width: 150px; height: 150px"></div>
        </div>
        <div class="{p}-cross"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></div>"""

TILE = """
    .{p}-cell { position: relative; width: 150px; height: 150px; background: #fff; border: 8px solid #0B2A30;
      box-shadow: 10px 10px 0 #0B2A30; font-size: 110px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 134px; text-align: center; }
    .{p}-cell.on { background: #FF5A1F; color: #fff; }
    .{p}-pv { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: -66px; font-size: 40px; line-height: 1; color: #2E6B63; font-weight: 700; }
"""

JS_HEAD = """
    const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
    const blurIn = (sel, t, d = 0.2) =>
      tl.fromTo(sel, { opacity: 0, filter: "blur(10px)" }, { opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)", duration: d, ease: "power2.out" }, t);
    const blurOut = (sel, t, d = 0.2) => tl.to(sel, { opacity: 0, filter: "blur(8px)", duration: d, ease: "power2.in" }, t);
    const land = (sel, t, from = 1.3, d = 0.35) =>
      tl.fromTo(sel, { opacity: 0, scale: from }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: d, ease: "expo.out" }, t);
"""


def scene(sid, p, dur, css, body, js):
    (C / f"{sid}.html").write_text(f"""<template>
  <style>{css.replace("{p}", p)}  </style>
  <div id="root" data-composition-id="{sid}" data-width="1920" data-height="1080">
    <div id="{p}-stage" class="clip {p}-stage" data-start="0" data-duration="{dur}">{body}
    </div>
  </div>
  <script>{JS_HEAD}{js}
    window.__timelines["{sid}"] = tl;
  </script>
</template>
""", encoding="utf-8")


def cells(p, bits, pv=False, prefix="", extra=""):
    out = []
    for i, b in enumerate(bits):
        place = [8, 4, 2, 1][i % 4]
        pvh = f'<span class="{p}-pv">{place}</span>' if pv else ""
        out.append(f'<div id="{prefix}{i}" class="{p}-cell{" on" if b == "1" else ""}">{pvh}{b}{extra}</div>')
    return "".join(out)


# ---- 1: HUD ----
p = "s1"
scene("hud", p, 8.5, ARENA, f"""
      <div id="s1-cam" class="{p}-cam" data-layout-allow-overflow>{ARENA_WORLD.replace("{p}", p)}
        <div id="s1-hud" class="{p}-hud">
          <div class="{p}-label">HEALTH</div>
          <div id="s1-num" class="{p}-num">100</div>
          <div class="{p}-bar"><div id="s1-fill" class="{p}-fill" style="width: 100%"></div></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="s1-white" style="position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #fff" data-layout-ignore></div>""", """
    // the world looks around a little, then the camera dives into the stem of the "1"
    tl.fromTo("#s1-world", { x: 60 }, { x: -40, duration: 5.2, ease: "sine.inOut" }, 0);
    tl.fromTo("#s1-fill", { clipPath: "inset(0 100% 0 0)" }, { clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)", duration: 0.9, ease: "power2.out" }, 0.25);
    const hp = { v: 0 };
    const num = document.querySelector("#s1-num");
    tl.fromTo(hp, { v: 0 }, { v: 100, duration: 0.9, ease: "power2.out", onUpdate: () => { num.textContent = Math.round(hp.v); } }, 0.25);
    gsap.set("#s1-cam", { transformOrigin: "345px 765px" });
    tl.fromTo("#s1-cam", { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.35, duration: 2.6, ease: "power2.inOut" }, 5.0);
    tl.to("#s1-cam", { scale: 5, duration: 0.9, ease: "power3.in" }, 7.6);
    // the white of the numeral opens over the frame
    tl.fromTo("#s1-white", { clipPath: "circle(0px at 345px 765px)" }, { clipPath: "circle(2000px at 345px 765px)", duration: 0.5, ease: "power3.in" }, 8.0);
""")

# ---- 2: memory wall ----
p = "s2"
rows = [
    ("00F8A480", "3C 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 9A 99 19 3F 00 00 80 3F"),
    ("00F8A490", "00 00 C8 42 00 00 48 43 00 00 20 41 14 00 00 00"),
    ("00F8A4A0", "28 00 00 00 02 00 01 00 E8 03 00 00 64 00 00 00"),
    ("00F8A4B0", "32 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 42 6F 62 00 00 00 00 00"),
    ("00F8A4C0", "FF FF FF FF 10 27 00 00 00 00 A0 40 01 01 00 00"),
    ("00F8A4D0", "00 20 3F 0A 00 00 00 00 0C 00 00 00 7F 00 00 00"),
    ("00F8A4E0", "05 00 00 00 00 00 7A 44 00 00 00 00 1E 00 00 00"),
]
rh = []
for n, (addr, bs) in enumerate(rows):
    bh = []
    for k, b in enumerate(bs.split()):
        hero = n == 2 and k == 12
        bh.append(f'<span id="s2-hero" class="s2-hero">{b}</span>' if hero else f'<span class="s2-b">{b}</span>')
    rh.append(f'        <div id="s2-row{n}" class="{p}-row"><span class="{p}-addr">{addr}</span>{"".join(bh)}</div>')
scene("wall", p, 9.1, PAPER + """
    .{p}-wall { position: absolute; left: 96px; top: 150px; right: 96px; }
    .{p}-row { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 112px; font-size: 56px; font-weight: 700; color: #0B2A30; }
    .{p}-row span { width: 96px; height: 96px; line-height: 96px; text-align: center; }
    .{p}-row .{p}-addr { width: 330px; text-align: left; color: #2E6B63; margin-right: 30px; }
    .{p}-flash { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #fff; }
""", f"""
      <div id="s2-wall" class="{p}-wall" data-layout-allow-overflow>
{chr(10).join(rh)}
      </div>
      <div id="s2-flash" class="{p}-flash" data-layout-ignore></div>""", """
    // out of the white of the numeral, rows print one at a time
    tl.fromTo("#s2-flash", { opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.3, ease: "power2.out" }, 0);
    for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
      tl.fromTo("#s2-row" + i, { clipPath: "inset(0 100% 0 0)" }, { clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)", duration: 0.45, ease: "power1.inOut" }, 1.0 + i * 0.38);
    }
    // everything dims except the byte we follow
    tl.to(".s2-b", { color: "#9DC4BA", duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.inOut" }, 5.8);
    tl.to(".s2-addr", { color: "#9DC4BA", duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.inOut" }, 5.8);
    tl.to("#s2-row2 .s2-addr", { color: "#2E6B63", duration: 0.3 }, 6.3);
    tl.fromTo("#s2-hero", { backgroundColor: "rgba(255,90,31,0)", color: "#0B2A30", scale: 1 },
      { backgroundColor: "rgba(255,90,31,1)", color: "#ffffff", scale: 1.25, duration: 0.3, ease: "back.out(2.5)" }, 6.1);
    // push in on it; the tile of the next scene takes over at this size and place
    gsap.set("#s2-wall", { transformOrigin: "1415px 280px" });
    tl.fromTo("#s2-wall", { scale: 1 }, { scale: 5.6, duration: 0.8, ease: "power3.in" }, 8.3);
""")

# ---- 3: the byte alone ----
p = "s3"
scene("byte", p, 9.6, PAPER + """
    .{p}-tile { position: absolute; left: 192px; top: 240px; width: 640px; height: 600px; background: #FF5A1F; color: #fff;
      border: 12px solid #0B2A30; box-shadow: 18px 18px 0 #0B2A30; font-size: 440px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 576px; text-align: center; }

        <div id="s2-row4" class="s2-row"><span class="s2-addr">00F8A4C0</span><span class="s2-b">FF</span><span class="s2-b">FF</span><span class="s2-b">FF</span><span class="s2-b">FF</span><span class="s2-b">10</span><span class="s2-b">27</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">A0</span><span class="s2-b">40</span><span class="s2-b">01</span><span class="s2-b">01</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span></div>
        <div id="s2-row5" class="s2-row"><span class="s2-addr">00F8A4D0</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">20</span><span class="s2-b">3F</span><span class="s2-b">0A</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">0C</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">7F</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span></div>
        <div id="s2-row6" class="s2-row"><span class="s2-addr">00F8A4E0</span><span class="s2-b">05</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">7A</span><span class="s2-b">44</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">1E</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span><span class="s2-b">00</span></div>
      </div>
      <div id="s2-flash" class="s2-flash" data-layout-ignore></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <script>
    const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
    const blurIn = (sel, t, d = 0.2) =>
      tl.fromTo(sel, { opacity: 0, filter: "blur(10px)" }, { opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)", duration: d, ease: "power2.out" }, t);
    const blurOut = (sel, t, d = 0.2) => tl.to(sel, { opacity: 0, filter: "blur(8px)", duration: d, ease: "power2.in" }, t);
    const land = (sel, t, from = 1.3, d = 0.35) =>
      tl.fromTo(sel, { opacity: 0, scale: from }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: d, ease: "expo.out" }, t);

    // out of the white of the numeral, rows print one at a time
    tl.fromTo("#s2-flash", { opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.3, ease: "power2.out" }, 0);
    for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
      tl.fromTo("#s2-row" + i, { clipPath: "inset(0 100% 0 0)" }, { clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)", duration: 0.45, ease: "power1.inOut" }, 1.0 + i * 0.38);
    }
    // everything dims except the byte we follow
    tl.to(".s2-b", { color: "#9DC4BA", duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.inOut" }, 5.8);
    tl.to(".s2-addr", { color: "#9DC4BA", duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.inOut" }, 5.8);
    tl.to("#s2-row2 .s2-addr", { color: "#2E6B63", duration: 0.3 }, 6.3);
    tl.fromTo("#s2-hero", { backgroundColor: "rgba(255,90,31,0)", color: "#0B2A30", scale: 1 },
      { backgroundColor: "rgba(255,90,31,1)", color: "#ffffff", scale: 1.25, duration: 0.3, ease: "back.out(2.5)" }, 6.1);
    // push in on it; the tile of the next scene takes over at this size and place
    gsap.set("#s2-wall", { transformOrigin: "1415px 280px" });
    tl.fromTo("#s2-wall", { scale: 1 }, { scale: 5.6, duration: 0.8, ease: "power3.in" }, 8.3);

    window.__timelines["wall"] = tl;
  </script>
</template>

`videos/02-data-types/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# HyperFrames Composition Project

This folder is a [HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) video: HTML, CSS and seekable
animations (GSAP by default) that the `hyperframes` CLI previews in the browser and renders to
MP4.

## Skills — read these first

**Invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that generic web docs don't cover, so compositions written without them break.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes`. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (each kind of film, story, motion, look, sound, review, captions, overlays). Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you.

- `/hyperframes` — read first for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays. Holds the render contract and the work loop.
- `/hyperframes-cli` — the CLI by job: scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render, publish, project history.
- `/hyperframes-registry` — ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source. Search it before hand-building any named visual.
- `/media-use` — get or make any media (music, sound effects, images, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades) and mix placed audio.
- `/reverse-any-video` — rebuild any video file as an editable HyperFrames project and check it against the original frame by frame (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/style-sampling` — make a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/figma` — bring a Figma design, frame, logo or brand into a video.
- `/slideshow` — a presentation or pitch deck. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4.
- `/remotion-to-hyperframes` — bring existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, or renders from other tools) and verify it frame by frame against the original.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `hyperframes-cli/references/init-and-scaffold.md` (Tailwind).

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. The person updates
> the plugin through its plugin manager; the standalone commands below do not apply.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Installing and updating skills is the person's step:
> tell them which skill is missing or stale, and do not run the install yourself. For the user:
> `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` installs/refreshes that skill, and bare
> `npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes the core set plus everything already installed —
> neither pulls the full set. Newly installed skills load in a new agent session.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # human-operated foreground preview (blocks until stopped)
npx hyperframes preview --background  # agent-safe persistent Studio preview
npx hyperframes preview --status      # verify the persistent preview is listening
npx hyperframes preview --stop        # stop it when review is finished
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npx hyperframes snapshot --at 1,3,5  # PNG frames at those seconds, to look at before rendering
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **Agents must use `npx hyperframes preview --background` for Studio handoff.** Do not rely
> on a shell/tool `run_in_background` wrapper around `npm run dev`: that foreground process
> remains owned by the invoking session and can disappear while the browser stays open,
> leaving refreshes at `ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`. Verify with `preview --status`. The desktop
> app can't edit the project while this preview runs, so `npx hyperframes open` stops it first.
> If you hand the project to the app another way, run `preview --stop` before you do. Otherwise keep it
> alive through review, and stop it explicitly with `preview --stop` afterward.

> **Back from the desktop app.** Once this project was opened in the HyperFrames desktop app, run `npx hyperframes catch-up` before your next change here: it lists what the person asked Framey in the app and which files changed since.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

Then look at what you changed: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>` (or `--range START,END`, `--composition <id>`) at the moments you edited, and read the frames before you reply. A passing check does not show how it looks.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start` and a duration. `data-start` is what marks it as timed; `data-track-index` is an optional Studio display lane the render never reads
2. Give timed visual elements `class="clip"`. The framework keys visibility off `data-start`, not the class, but the shared `.clip` CSS is what gives a scene its full-frame box, and `lint` warns without it
3. Register one paused root timeline per composition on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
   Scene timelines manually added to this root must not be paused. A paused
   child does not advance when the root is seeked. The runtime activates
   registered composition siblings, not arbitrary nested scene timelines.
4. A video with sound keeps it on the `<video>` (`data-has-audio="true"`, no `muted`). Use a separate `<audio>` for music, voiceover, replacement audio, J/L cuts, or audio detached in Studio. Silent footage and b-roll: `muted`.
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

```

`videos/02-data-types/SCRIPT.md`:

```md
# Narration: Same Bytes, Different Number

Voiced with Azure Speech (en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural, rate -4%). Generated by build.py.

1. (0.0–9.6) You search the game's memory for your health, one hundred. Zero results. The number is right there on screen. So where is it?
2. (9.6–16.4) It is here, in these four bytes. They just don't say one hundred the way you expected.
3. (16.4–24.1) Read them as a whole number and you get one billion, one hundred twenty million. Nonsense for a health bar.
4. (24.1–32.1) Read the same four bytes as a float, a number with a decimal point, and they say exactly one hundred.
5. (32.1–43.8) A whole number one hundred looks completely different: sixty-four, zero, zero, zero. Same value on screen, different bytes in memory.
6. (43.8–55.1) And the bytes run backwards. One thousand is hex three E eight, but memory stores the small end first: E eight, zero three.
7. (55.1–64.0) So when a search finds nothing, change the type. Whole numbers for things you count. Floats for things that move.
8. (64.0–71.6) Memory holds only bytes. The type is how you choose to read them.

```

`videos/02-data-types/build.py`:

```py
"""Video 2: Same Bytes, Different Number (data types in memory).  Run: python build.py"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tools"))
from kit import Scene, arena, bar, build, card, cells, tile, txt  # noqa: E402,F401

B = ["00", "00", "C8", "42"]

scenes = [
    Scene("hook", "You search the game's memory for your health, one hundred. Zero results. "
                  "The number is right there on screen. So where is it?",
          bg="arena",
          body=arena("100")
          + card("@p-q", 1010, 150, 720, 120, "search: 100 &nbsp;(4 Bytes)", 50)
          + card("@p-r", 1010, 310, 720, 120, "0 results", 60, "on"),
          js="""
    land("#@p-q", <<search>>);
    land("#@p-r", <<zero>>);
    tl.fromTo("#@p-hudn", { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.08, duration: 0.2, ease: "power2.out", yoyo: true, repeat: 1 }, <<screen>>);
    tl.fromTo("#@p-r", { rotation: 0 }, { rotation: -3, duration: 0.25, ease: "power2.out" }, <<where>>);
"""),

    Scene("four", "It is here, in these four bytes. They just don't say one hundred the way you expected.",
          body=txt("@p-t", 475, 250, "your health, as the game stores it", "m")
          + cells("@p-b", 475, 380, B, 220, 30, on={0, 1, 2, 3})
          + txt("@p-u", 475, 680, "4 bytes &middot; no label &middot; no type", "m"),
          js="""
    each(".c-@p-b", <<here>>, 0.15);
    blurIn("#@p-t", <<four>>);
    blurIn("#@p-u", <<they>>);
"""),

    Scene("asint", "Read them as a whole number and you get one billion, one hundred twenty million. "
                   "Nonsense for a health bar.",
          body=cells("@p-b", 564, 150, B, 180, 24, on={0, 1, 2, 3})
          + txt("@p-l", 0, 400, "read as a whole number (4 Bytes)", "m", w=1920, align="center")
          + txt("@p-n", 0, 510, "1,120,403,456", "h", fs=190, w=1920, align="center")
          + txt("@p-c", 0, 790, "nonsense for a health bar", "m", w=1920, align="center"),
          js="""
    blurIn("#@p-l", <<whole>>);
    land("#@p-n", <<billion-0.4>>);
    blurIn("#@p-c", <<nonsense>>);
"""),

    Scene("asfloat", "Read the same four bytes as a float, a number with a decimal point, "
                     "and they say exactly one hundred.",
          body=cells("@p-b", 564, 150, B, 180, 24, on={0, 1, 2, 3})
          + txt("@p-l", 0, 400, "read as a float", "m", w=1920, align="center")
          + txt("@p-n", 0, 500, '<span class="@p-acc">100.0</span>', "h", fs=260, w=1920, align="center")
          + txt("@p-c", 0, 830, "a number with a decimal point", "m", w=1920, align="center"),
          js="""
    blurIn("#@p-l", <<float>>);
    blurIn("#@p-c", <<decimal-0.4>>);
    land("#@p-n", <<exactly>>);
"""),

    Scene("compare", "A whole number one hundred looks completely different: sixty-four, zero, zero, zero. "
                     "Same value on screen, different bytes in memory.",
          body=txt("@p-la", 190, 290, "100 as a<br>whole number", "m")
          + cells("@p-a", 860, 250, ["64", "00", "00", "00"], 170, 22, on={0})
          + txt("@p-lb", 190, 580, "100.0 as a<br>float", "m")
          + cells("@p-b", 860, 540, B, 170, 22, on={2, 3})
          + txt("@p-f", 0, 830, "same number on screen &middot; different bytes", "h", fs=76, w=1920, align="center"),
          js="""
    blurIn("#@p-la", <<whole>>);
    each(".c-@p-a", <<sixty-four>>, 0.4);
    blurIn("#@p-lb", <<same-0.3>>);
    each(".c-@p-b", <<same>>, 0.12);
    blurIn("#@p-f", <<different#2-0.2>>);
"""),

    Scene("endian", "And the bytes run backwards. One thousand is hex three E eight, "
                    "but memory stores the small end first: E eight, zero three.",
          body=txt("@p-t", 0, 150, '1000 = 0x0000<span class="@p-acc">03E8</span>', "h", fs=120, w=1920, align="center")
          + txt("@p-l", 0, 400, "in memory", "m", w=1920, align="center")
          + cells("@p-b", 515, 500, ["E8", "03", "00", "00"], 200, 30, on={0, 1})
          + txt("@p-c", 0, 800, "small end first: little-endian", "m", w=1920, align="center"),
          js="""
    land("#@p-t", <<thousand-0.4>>);
    blurIn("#@p-l", <<memory>>);
    blurIn("#@p-c", <<small>>);
    each(".c-@p-b", <<first+0.4>>, 0.35);
"""),

    Scene("rule", "So when a search finds nothing, change the type. Whole numbers for things you count. "
                  "Floats for things that move.",
          body=txt("@p-t", 190, 90, "no results? change the type.", "h", fs=84)
          + txt("@p-lh", 190, 260, "things you count", "m")
          + card("@p-l0", 190, 350, 520, 100, "ammo") + card("@p-l1", 190, 480, 520, 100, "money")
          + card("@p-l2", 190, 610, 520, 100, "score")
          + tile("@p-lt", 190, 770, 520, 150, "4 Bytes", 76)
          + txt("@p-rh", 1010, 260, "things that move", "m")
          + card("@p-r0", 1010, 350, 520, 100, "position") + card("@p-r1", 1010, 480, 520, 100, "speed")
          + card("@p-r2", 1010, 610, 520, 100, "angle")
          + tile("@p-rt", 1010, 770, 520, 150, "Float", 76),
          js="""
    wipe("#@p-t", <<change-0.3>>, 0.4);
    land("#@p-lt", <<whole>>);
    blurIn("#@p-lh", <<things>>);
    each(["#@p-l0", "#@p-l1", "#@p-l2"], <<things+0.1>>, 0.14);
    land("#@p-rt", <<floats>>);
    blurIn("#@p-rh", <<things#2>>);
    each(["#@p-r0", "#@p-r1", "#@p-r2"], <<things#2+0.1>>, 0.14);
"""),

    Scene("claim", "Memory holds only bytes. The type is how you choose to read them.",
          body=cells("@p-b", 192, 190, B, 120, 18, on={0, 1, 2, 3})
          + txt("@p-a", 192, 400, "Memory holds only bytes.", "h", fs=118)
          + txt("@p-c", 192, 540, '<span class="@p-acc">The type is how you read them.</span>', "h", fs=96),
          js="""
    each(".c-@p-b", 0.3, 0.08);
    wipe("#@p-a", <<memory>>, 0.5);
    wipe("#@p-c", <<type-0.2>>, 0.6);
"""),
]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    build(__file__, scenes, "Same Bytes, Different Number")

```

# HyperFrames Composition Project

This folder is a [HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) video: HTML, CSS and seekable
animations (GSAP by default) that the `hyperframes` CLI previews in the browser and renders to
MP4.

## Skills — read these first

**Invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that generic web docs don't cover, so compositions written without them break.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes`. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (each kind of film, story, motion, look, sound, review, captions, overlays). Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you.

- `/hyperframes` — read first for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays. Holds the render contract and the work loop.
- `/hyperframes-cli` — the CLI by job: scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render, publish, project history.
- `/hyperframes-registry` — ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source. Search it before hand-building any named visual.
- `/media-use` — get or make any media (music, sound effects, images, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades) and mix placed audio.
- `/reverse-any-video` — rebuild any video file as an editable HyperFrames project and check it against the original frame by frame (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/style-sampling` — make a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/figma` — bring a Figma design, frame, logo or brand into a video.
- `/slideshow` — a presentation or pitch deck. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4.
- `/remotion-to-hyperframes` — bring existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, or renders from other tools) and verify it frame by frame against the original.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `hyperframes-cli/references/init-and-scaffold.md` (Tailwind).

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. The person updates
> the plugin through its plugin manager; the standalone commands below do not apply.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Installing and updating skills is the person's step:
> tell them which skill is missing or stale, and do not run the install yourself. For the user:
> `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` installs/refreshes that skill, and bare
> `npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes the core set plus everything already installed —
> neither pulls the full set. Newly installed skills load in a new agent session.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # human-operated foreground preview (blocks until stopped)
npx hyperframes preview --background  # agent-safe persistent Studio preview
npx hyperframes preview --status      # verify the persistent preview is listening
npx hyperframes preview --stop        # stop it when review is finished
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npx hyperframes snapshot --at 1,3,5  # PNG frames at those seconds, to look at before rendering
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **Agents must use `npx hyperframes preview --background` for Studio handoff.** Do not rely
> on a shell/tool `run_in_background` wrapper around `npm run dev`: that foreground process
> remains owned by the invoking session and can disappear while the browser stays open,
> leaving refreshes at `ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`. Verify with `preview --status`. The desktop
> app can't edit the project while this preview runs, so `npx hyperframes open` stops it first.
> If you hand the project to the app another way, run `preview --stop` before you do. Otherwise keep it
> alive through review, and stop it explicitly with `preview --stop` afterward.

> **Back from the desktop app.** Once this project was opened in the HyperFrames desktop app, run `npx hyperframes catch-up` before your next change here: it lists what the person asked Framey in the app and which files changed since.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

Then look at what you changed: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>` (or `--range START,END`, `--composition <id>`) at the moments you edited, and read the frames before you reply. A passing check does not show how it looks.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start` and a duration. `data-start` is what marks it as timed; `data-track-index` is an optional Studio display lane the render never reads
2. Give timed visual elements `class="clip"`. The framework keys visibility off `data-start`, not the class, but the shared `.clip` CSS is what gives a scene its full-frame box, and `lint` warns without it
3. Register one paused root timeline per composition on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
   Scene timelines manually added to this root must not be paused. A paused
   child does not advance when the root is seeked. The runtime activates
   registered composition siblings, not arbitrary nested scene timelines.
4. A video with sound keeps it on the `<video>` (`data-has-audio="true"`, no `muted`). Use a separate `<audio>` for music, voiceover, replacement audio, J/L cuts, or audio detached in Studio. Silent footage and b-roll: `muted`.
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

```

`videos/03-virtual-memory/SCRIPT.md`:

```md
# Narration: Why the Address Changes

Voiced with Azure Speech (en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural, rate -4%). Generated by build.py.

1. (0.0–11.0) Yesterday you found your health at this address. Today you restart the game, and the same address holds garbage. Nothing broke. It moved.
2. (11.0–20.4) Every process lives in its own private map of memory. The same address in two programs is two different places.
3. (20.4–32.0) The map has regions. The game's own file, loaded as a module. The heap, where it creates things while running. And a stack for every thread.
4. (32.0–41.6) Each page of memory carries permissions. Code can be read and run, but not written. Data can be written, but not run.
5. (41.6–47.9) Your player is created on the heap, so it lands somewhere new on every run.
6. (47.9–56.3) Even the module moves. Windows loads it at a random base each time. That is A S L R.
7. (56.3–64.9) But the distance from the start of the module never changes. Base plus offset finds the same spot every time.
8. (64.9–72.5) Never save an address. Save the module and the offset.

```

```py
"""Video 3: Why the Address Changes (virtual memory).  Run: python build.py"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tools"))
from kit import Scene, bar, build, card, cells, tile, txt  # noqa: E402,F401

scenes = [
    Scene("hook", "Yesterday you found your health at this address. Today you restart the game, "
                  "and the same address holds garbage. Nothing broke. It moved.",
          body=txt("@p-lm", 250, 230, "yesterday", "m")
          + card("@p-la", 250, 320, 640, 130, "0x0A3F2000", 60)
          + txt("@p-lv", 250, 490, "= 100", "h", fs=170)
          + txt("@p-rm", 1030, 230, "today, after a restart", "m")
          + card("@p-ra", 1030, 320, 640, 130, "0x0A3F2000", 60)
          + txt("@p-rv", 1030, 490, '<span class="@p-acc">= ???</span>', "h", fs=170)
          + txt("@p-q", 250, 790, "nothing broke. it moved.", "h", fs=96),
          js="""
    land("#@p-la", <<found>>);
    land("#@p-lv", <<health>>);
    blurIn("#@p-rm", <<today>>);
    land("#@p-ra", <<restart>>);
    land("#@p-rv", <<garbage>>);
    wipe("#@p-q", <<nothing>>, 0.6);
"""),

    Scene("private", "Every process lives in its own private map of memory. "
                     "The same address in two programs is two different places.",
          body=txt("@p-l1", 250, 140, "game.exe", "m")
          + card("@p-m1", 250, 220, 600, 640, "", 40, "soft")
          + card("@p-a1", 320, 400, 460, 110, "0x00401000", 50)
          + txt("@p-c1", 320, 560, "game code", "m")
          + txt("@p-l2", 1070, 140, "notepad.exe", "m")
          + card("@p-m2", 1070, 220, 600, 640, "", 40, "soft")
          + card("@p-a2", 1140, 400, 460, 110, "0x00401000", 50)
          + txt("@p-c2", 1140, 560, "text editor code", "m"),
          js="""
    land("#@p-m1", <<process>>, 1.1);
    blurIn("#@p-l1", <<process>>);
    land("#@p-m2", <<private>>, 1.1);
    blurIn("#@p-l2", <<private>>);
    each(["#@p-a1", "#@p-a2"], <<same>>, 0.25);
    blurIn("#@p-c1", <<two#2>>);
    blurIn("#@p-c2", <<different>>);
"""),

    Scene("regions", "The map has regions. The game's own file, loaded as a module. "
                     "The heap, where it creates things while running. And a stack for every thread.",
          body=card("@p-r0", 260, 150, 620, 150, "game.exe", 60, "on")
          + txt("@p-d0", 980, 190, "the game's own file", "m")
          + card("@p-r1", 260, 330, 620, 130, "DLLs", 56)
          + txt("@p-d1", 980, 365, "more modules", "m")
          + card("@p-r2", 260, 490, 620, 200, "heap", 60, "soft")
          + txt("@p-d2", 980, 555, "things created while running", "m")
          + card("@p-r3", 260, 720, 620, 150, "stack", 60)
          + txt("@p-d3", 980, 760, "one for every thread", "m"),
          js="""
    land("#@p-r0", <<file>>);
    blurIn("#@p-d0", <<module>>);
    land("#@p-r1", <<module+0.6>>);
    blurIn("#@p-d1", <<module+0.8>>);
    land("#@p-r2", <<heap>>);
    blurIn("#@p-d2", <<creates>>);
    land("#@p-r3", <<stack>>);
    blurIn("#@p-d3", <<every>>);
"""),

    Scene("perms", "Each page of memory carries permissions. Code can be read and run, but not written. "
                   "Data can be written, but not run.",
          body=txt("@p-t", 190, 90, "every page has permissions", "h", fs=84)
          + card("@p-n0", 190, 280, 360, 130, ".text", 60) + card("@p-p0", 590, 280, 300, 130, "R X", 64, "on")
          + txt("@p-m0", 950, 315, "code: read and run, never write", "m", fs=46)
          + card("@p-n1", 190, 480, 360, 130, ".data", 60) + card("@p-p1", 590, 480, 300, 130, "R W", 64, "on")

          + card("@p-n2", 190, 680, 360, 130, ".rdata", 60) + card("@p-p2", 590, 680, 300, 130, "R", 64, "on")
          + txt("@p-m2", 950, 715, "constants: read only", "m", fs=46),

"""),

    Scene("heap", "Your player is created on the heap, so it lands somewhere new on every run.",

          + txt("@p-l1", 190, 345, "run 1", "m")
          + card("@p-h1", 420, 300, 1250, 170, "", 40, "soft")
          + card("@p-g1", 450, 320, 520, 130, "game.exe", 54, "on")
          + txt("@p-b1", 1010, 350, "base 0x00400000", "m")
          + txt("@p-l2", 190, 645, "run 2", "m")
          + card("@p-h2", 420, 600, 1250, 170, "", 40, "soft")
          + card("@p-g2", 1120, 620, 520, 130, "game.exe", 54, "on")
          + txt("@p-b2", 470, 650, "base 0x00D20000", "m"),
          js="""
    land("#@p-g1", <<module>>);
    blurIn("#@p-b1", <<moves>>);
    land("#@p-g2", <<random>>);
    blurIn("#@p-b2", <<base>>);
    wipe("#@p-t", <<that>>, 0.6);
"""),

    Scene("offset", "But the distance from the start of the module never changes. "
                    "Base plus offset finds the same spot every time.",
          body=txt("@p-r1", 190, 170, "run 1", "m")
          + txt("@p-l1", 190, 250, '0x00400000 + <span class="@p-acc">0x18AC00</span> = 0x0058AC00', "m", fs=70, color="#0B2A30")
          + txt("@p-r2", 190, 420, "run 2", "m")
          + txt("@p-l2", 190, 500, '0x00D20000 + <span class="@p-acc">0x18AC00</span> = 0x00EAAC00', "m", fs=70, color="#0B2A30")
          + tile("@p-k", 400, 730, 1120, 170, "game.exe + 0x18AC00", 76),
          js="""
    blurIn(["#@p-r1", "#@p-l1"], <<distance>>);
    blurIn(["#@p-r2", "#@p-l2"], <<never>>);
    land("#@p-k", <<base>>);
    tl.fromTo("#@p-k", { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.06, duration: 0.2, ease: "power2.out", yoyo: true, repeat: 1 }, <<every>>);
"""),

    Scene("claim", "Never save an address. Save the module and the offset.",
          body=card("@p-g", 192, 200, 520, 120, "game.exe", 54, "on")

    blurIn("#@p-o", 0.6);

"""),
]

if __name__ == "__main__":

  <div id="root" data-composition-id="regions" data-width="1920" data-height="1080">
    <div id="s3-stage" class="clip s3-stage" data-start="0" data-duration="11.6">
      <div id="s3-r0" class="s3-card on" style="left: 260px; top: 150px; width: 620px; height: 150px; line-height: 134px; font-size: 60px">game.exe</div>
      <div id="s3-d0" class="s3-m" style="left: 980px; top: 190px">the game's own file</div>
      <div id="s3-r1" class="s3-card " style="left: 260px; top: 330px; width: 620px; height: 130px; line-height: 114px; font-size: 56px">DLLs</div>
      <div id="s3-d1" class="s3-m" style="left: 980px; top: 365px">more modules</div>
      <div id="s3-r2" class="s3-card soft" style="left: 260px; top: 490px; width: 620px; height: 200px; line-height: 184px; font-size: 60px">heap</div>
      <div id="s3-d2" class="s3-m" style="left: 980px; top: 555px">things created while running</div>
      <div id="s3-r3" class="s3-card " style="left: 260px; top: 720px; width: 620px; height: 150px; line-height: 134px; font-size: 60px">stack</div>
      <div id="s3-d3" class="s3-m" style="left: 980px; top: 760px">one for every thread</div>
    </div>
